key_developments: Iowa and Texas Senate races shifted to toss-up status, expanding Democrats' path to Senate control as Trump economy concerns affect rural voters.
Progressive Abdul El-Sayed narrowly won Michigan Democratic Senate primary over centrist Haley Stevens, setting up general election against Republican Mike Rogers in key battleground.
Wisconsin gubernatorial race emerging as competitive, with Democrat David Crowley holding narrow lead over Republican Tom Tiffany in post-primary polling.
Democratic turnout appears strong heading into November despite internal party divisions, contradicting historical patterns of midterm fatigue.
Trump's primary victories over incumbents including Cornyn and Cassidy may create general election vulnerabilities in competitive districts.

senate.label: Michigan Senate
senate.note: Abdul El-Sayed (D) leads Rogers 48-47 per AARP poll but struggles with voters 50+ in this deadlocked race.

senate.label: Iowa Senate
senate.note: Race increasingly competitive as Trump economy hurts agricultural voters; shifted from solid Republican to toss-up.

senate.label: Texas Senate
senate.note: Cook Political Report downgraded race from safe to toss-up, representing significant Democratic opportunity in Trump stronghold.

senate.label: Georgia Senate
senate.note: Democrats defending Trump-won state but within striking distance; part of critical battleground holding pattern.

house.label: Wisconsin 3rd District
house.note: David Crowley holds narrow Democratic lead in first post-primary poll of this competitive House race.

house.label: Ohio 13th District
house.note: Cook Political Report downgraded from Solid Republican to Likely Republican, indicating Democratic competitiveness.

house.label: Colorado 3rd District
